extractor: read directly from the official GOV.UK pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state. A business visit is made on a Standard Visitor visa, so the application, evidence and fee entries are read from the shared Standard Visitor apply page and the business-specific conditions from the 'visit on business' chapter. The UK publishes no application form identifier for this route, so official_form_code is null everywhere.
not_extracted: The registered 'forms' source https://visas-immigration.service.gov.uk/product/uk-visit-visa was NOT fetched. That host's robots.txt is 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: /', so the whole site is off limits to the monitor. It is therefore absent from source_roles and no requirement cites it.

The general Standard Visitor eligibility requirements (valid travel document, leaving at the end of the visit, supporting yourself, paying for the return journey, not living in the UK by successive visits). The business page tells you to check them but states them on the /standard-visitor overview page, which is not a registered source for this visa type. They are extracted in full under gb-standard-visitor-visa.
The Immigration Rules' visitor rules appendix, which the business page links to for what each overseas job role may do in the UK. It is a separate document, not a registered source.
The rules for a 'permitted paid engagement', including who counts as an expert and which engagements may be paid — unregistered sub-page /standard-visitor/visit-for-a-paid-engagement.
The 'manufacture and supply of goods to the UK' contract rules, which the business page links out to.
The list of nationalities that need a visa, an ETA, or neither — behind GOV.UK's separate checker tool.
The Visitor in Transit visa fee, priority service fees, and the healthcare surcharge — none is stated for this route on a registered page.

requirements.label: Do business activities only if you are not paid by a UK-based organisation or client
requirements.source_excerpt: you can visit the uk as a standard visitor for up to 6 months: to do certain business activities, if you are not paid by a uk-based organisation or client
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You can visit the UK as a Standard Visitor for up to 6 months: to do certain business activities, if you are not paid by a UK-based organisation or client

requirements.label: Do only the permitted business activities
requirements.description: GOV.UK lists: attend interviews, meetings, conferences and seminars; negotiate and sign deals and contracts; attend trade fairs to promote your business (you cannot sell things); get work-related training if you are employed overseas and the training is not available in your home country; give a one-off or short series of talks that are not for profit or a commercial event; carry out site visits and inspections; oversee delivery of goods and services provided by a UK company to your overseas company; deliver training or share knowledge on internal projects with UK employees of the company you work for overseas; and carry out specific activities where your overseas employer has an eligible contract of purchase, supply or lease with a UK company.
requirements.source_excerpt: you can visit the uk as a standard visitor to do the following business activities if you’re not paid by a uk-based organisation or client: attend interviews, meetings, conferences and seminars
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You can visit the UK as a Standard Visitor to do the following business activities if you’re not paid by a UK-based organisation or client: attend interviews, meetings, conferences and seminars

requirements.label: Any other paid or unpaid work needs a work visa, not a visitor visa
requirements.source_excerpt: you’ll need to apply for a work visa if you want to do any other paid or unpaid work in the uk.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You’ll need to apply for a work visa if you want to do any other paid or unpaid work in the UK.

requirements.label: Paid work is allowed only as a permitted paid engagement, as an expert in your profession
requirements.description: The rules for permitted paid engagements are on a separate GOV.UK sub-page that is not a registered source, so their contents are not extracted here.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you are visiting as an expert in your profession to do a permitted paid engagement
requirements.source_excerpt_display: if you are visiting as an expert in your profession to do a permitted paid engagement

requirements.label: Extra activities are allowed in certain overseas job roles
requirements.description: GOV.UK names archaeologists; artists, entertainers or musicians; bodyguards; camera operators; drivers; internal auditors; journalists or correspondents; lawyers or expert witnesses; market researchers or analysts; personal assistants; pilots or cabin crew on a CAA-approved wet lease agreement between 1 March and 31 October; professors from an overseas academic institution; religious workers; scientists or researchers; seafarers; sports people or sports officials; tour group couriers; translators or interpreters; film crew including actors, producers, directors and technicians; production team members supporting an artist, entertainer or musician; and technical staff supporting an artist, entertainer, musician or sports person. What each role may actually do is set out in the visitor rules, which are not a registered source.
requirements.source_excerpt: you can do certain additional activities in the uk as a standard visitor, if you’re employed overseas as: an archaeologist
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You can do certain additional activities in the UK as a Standard Visitor, if you’re employed overseas as: an archaeologist

requirements.label: Passport or travel document valid for the whole of your stay in the UK
requirements.source_excerpt: you must have a passport or travel document that is valid for the whole of your stay in the uk.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must have a passport or travel document that is valid for the whole of your stay in the UK.

requirements.label: Extra details some applicants must give, depending on circumstances
requirements.description: GOV.UK lists these under "depending on your circumstances, you might also need to provide": details of your travel history for the past 10 years; your employer's address and telephone number; your partner's name, date of birth and passport number; the name and address of anyone paying for your trip; the name, address and passport number of any family members you have in the UK. For a business visitor the employer's contact details and the name and address of whoever is paying for the trip are the ones most often reached for, but the page states no rule for which apply to whom.
requirements.source_excerpt: depending on your circumstances, you might also need to provide: details of your travel history for the past 10 years
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Depending on your circumstances, you might also need to provide: details of your travel history for the past 10 years

requirements.description: GOV.UK ties this to a visit of more than 6 months.
requirements.source_excerpt: a certificate proving that you’ve had a tuberculosis ( tb ) test if you’re visiting for more than 6 months
requirements.source_excerpt_display: a certificate proving that you’ve had a tuberculosis (TB) test if you’re visiting for more than 6 months

requirements.label: Certified translations of documents not in English or Welsh
requirements.source_excerpt: you must provide certified translations of any documents that are not in english or welsh.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must provide certified translations of any documents that are not in English or Welsh.

requirements.label: Check the basic Standard Visitor eligibility requirements and whether you need a visa
requirements.description: Whether you need a Standard Visitor visa, an ETA, or neither depends on your nationality, and GOV.UK publishes that only through its separate checker tool.
requirements.source_excerpt: you should: check you meet the basic eligibility requirements for a standard visitor ... check if you need a visa to visit the uk ... apply for a standard visitor visa online - if you need one
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You should: check you meet the basic eligibility requirements for a Standard Visitor ... check if you need a visa to visit the UK ... apply for a Standard Visitor visa online - if you need one

requirements.label: Apply online before you travel, and book an appointment at a visa application centre
requirements.description: The UK publishes no application form number for this route — the application exists only as an online service. GOV.UK also states you can save the form and finish it later, and that each person travelling needs their own application, fee and appointment.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you need a standard visitor visa, you must apply online before you travel to the uk and attend an appointment at a visa application centre. the earliest you can apply is 3 months before you travel.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you need a Standard Visitor visa, you must apply online before you travel to the UK and attend an appointment at a visa application centre. The earliest you can apply is 3 months before you travel.

requirements.label: Give the required information in your online application
requirements.description: GOV.UK lists: the dates you're planning to travel to the UK; where you'll be staying during your visit; how much you think your trip will cost; your current home address and how long you've lived there; your parents' names and dates of birth (if known); how much you earn in a year (if you have an income); details of any criminal, civil or immigration offences you may have committed.
requirements.source_excerpt: you’ll need to provide the following information in your online application: the dates you’re planning to travel to the uk
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You’ll need to provide the following information in your online application: the dates you’re planning to travel to the UK

requirements.label: Prove your identity and give biometrics at a visa application centre
requirements.description: GOV.UK notes the visa application centre could be in another country, that your passport is returned the same day, and that the centre may keep some of your other documents while the application is processed.
requirements.source_excerpt: at your appointment, you’ll need to: prove your identity with your passport or travel document ... have your fingerprints and a photo (biometric information) taken ... provide the required documents that show you’re eligible for a standard visitor visa
requirements.source_excerpt_display: At your appointment, you’ll need to: prove your identity with your passport or travel document ... have your fingerprints and a photo (biometric information) taken ... provide the required documents that show you’re eligible for a Standard Visitor visa

requirements.label: Standard Visitor visa application fee
requirements.description: A business visit is made on a Standard Visitor visa and pays the same fees. GOV.UK publishes six tiers: GBP 135 for up to 6 months; GBP 234 for a visit for medical reasons (11 months) and GBP 234 for academics (12 months); and the long-term visitor visas at GBP 506 (2 years), GBP 903 (5 years) and GBP 1,128 (10 years), each allowing a maximum stay of 6 months per visit. Each person applying pays their own fee.

tiers.tier: standard visitor visa for medical reasons
